\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models on three reasoning domains with over 3,000 condition-evaluations across ${\sim}$1,250 unique instances. Beyond accuracy comparisons, we conduct diagnostic analyses of symbolic confirmation bias and process-level trace independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B parameters).

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold FOL annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$; extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$. Z3 timeout: 10s. $\alpha{=}0.5$. Statistical significance via McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs from 10,000 resamples for $n \geq 200$.

\paragraph{Computational cost.} On Mistral-7B FOLIO ($K{=}12$), SICA takes $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock time; constraint extraction ($K$ additional LLM calls) accounts for 76\% of overhead, Z3 solving is negligible (${<}0.1\%$).


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all conditions sorted by SC baseline. We identify three empirical regimes (thresholds observation-driven, not theoretically derived). SICA effectiveness depends sharply on this accuracy regime.

Failure modes detailed in Appendix~\ref{app:failure-modes}.}

\paragraph{Intermediate-SC region.} Mistral-7B on FOLIO (SC $\sim$50--55\%) shows positive directional trends in 2 of 4 seeds: $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.092$) and $+2.94$\,pp ($p = 0.070$); the remaining seeds show null or negative results. No seed reaches $p < 0.05$; the 4-seed mean is $+1.47$\,pp. The default-seed and seed-456 runs share identical SC baselines (55.88\%) yet diverge ($+3.43$ vs.\ $0.00$\,pp), suggesting that seed-level constraint quality, not SC level alone, influences the effect (entropy decomposition in Appendix~\ref{app:entropy}). Mistral-7B on LogiQA, despite the same SC range, yields only $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), attributable to domain formalizability (Appendix~\ref{app:failure-modes}).

\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ 60\%): confirmation bias.} All nine Type~A conditions (SC $\geq 60\%$, combined $N > 2{,}800$) produce no significant positive effects. The largest positive trend is LLaMA-3.1-8B on StrategyQA ($\Delta = +2.00$\,pp, $p = 0.424$, n.s.), while Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter shows significant degradation ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$). Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples ($\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, n.s.) cannot break confirmation bias.

\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ 40\%): error amplification.} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} by formalizing incorrect reasoning.

\paragraph{Degenerate cases.} When $C_0 < 5\%$, nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction.

\paragraph{Equivalence testing.} TOST equivalence tests \citep{lakens2017equivalence} with margin $\pm 2$\,pp establish equivalence for 4 of 15 non-degenerate conditions; 5 show genuine SICA--SC differences (4 negative, 1 positive n.s.); the remaining 6 are underpowered (Appendix~\ref{app:tost}).


\subsection{Oracle Control}
\label{sec:oracle}

Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and DSL from ProofWriter ($n = 600$), where depth-stratified rules are programmatically derived, requiring no human annotation. Same-model Oracle-SICA on Mistral-7B achieves 85.78\% on FOLIO ($\Delta = +29.90$\,pp, $p < 10^{-13}$); Qwen2.5-14B achieves 89.71\% ($\Delta = +14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$) and 86.67\% on ProofWriter ($\Delta = +11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% (FOLIO) and 97.1\% (ProofWriter) of problems. The larger ceiling for weaker models ($+29.90$ vs.\ $+14.22$\,pp) is consistent with the bias ratio gradient (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).

These results establish that the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound given discriminative constraints. Mistral-7B's best self-extracted result ($+3.43$\,pp) captures only 11.5\% of its same-model oracle ceiling ($+29.90$\,pp). The remaining ${\sim}$88\% is lost to self-extraction quality.

Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts first-order logic (FOL) constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), we find that self-extracted constraints do not improve majority voting: none of fifteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect; TOST equivalence tests (margin $\pm 2$\,pp) establish equivalence for four conditions, while five show genuine SICA--SC differences---four of which are negative.
We identify \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} as the root cause: on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC.
Process-level analysis reveals a deeper bottleneck: chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level Fleiss' $\kappa$ ($0.41$), indicating that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on answers.
Twenty-plus same-model remediation strategies spanning fifteen families all fail, revealing a persistent independence-accuracy trade-off at the 7B--32B scale: methods that increase trace independence destroy accuracy (Debate: $\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp), while methods preserving accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$ across three model families).
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+29.90$\,pp and $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter; $p < 0.001$); same-model self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of the oracle ceiling.
However, a cross-architecture proof-of-concept---DeBERTa-large NLI combined with SC---shows consistent positive effects across two datasets ($+3.50$\,pp on ProofWriter, $p = 0.013$; McNemar exact test), suggesting that the oracle gap is partially recoverable when verification signal comes from outside the reasoning model's distribution.

674	\paragraph{Contrastive discordant analysis.} Contrastive produces 34 discordant questions on FOLIO. All 34 produced non-degenerate scores (both pro and con constraint sets non-empty), compared to 20.1\% degenerate scores in the full sample. This indicates that scoring failures on discordant questions stem from systematic pro-bias rather than missing constraints. Among discordant questions, 97.1\% contain negation words in the problem statement versus 76.5\% in the full sample, suggesting that negation-bearing problems are particularly susceptible to pro-constraint imbalance. \toprule
Model & Single Trace & SC@12 (\%) & Agg.\ Gain (pp) \\
\midrule

> "At the thinking-mode frontier, a single trace achieves 83.28%, leaving SC@12 only 0.45pp of headroom. The Symbolic Mirage is not merely a constraint-extraction failure; it reflects a deeper saturation: as models internalize reasoning, the marginal value of any test-time aggregation---symbolic or otherwise---approaches zero."

---

### §6.2 Theoretical: The Mirage Explains Both Endpoints

**Opening**: The Symbolic Mirage framework (§3.3) provides a unified explanation for both endpoints of the capability spectrum.

**Low-capability (Mistral-7B)**:
- BR = 4.97×, oracle gap = +29.90pp (FOLIO)
- Aggregation gain exists (+8.00pp SC over single) but is locked by confirmation bias
- SICA captures only ~12% of oracle ceiling → self-extracted constraints cannot unlock the remaining 88%
- Δ_max ≤ OracleGap / BR ≈ 6.0pp; observed +3.43pp (best seed)

**High-capability (Qwen3-14B thinking)**:
- κ = 0.91, K_eff = 1.09 → 12 traces ≈ 1 independent vote
- Inter-trace std = 0.99% (vs Mistral's 2.80%) → diversity already consumed by training
- Oracle gap ≈ 3pp [PENDING Dir-N for exact number] → ceiling itself is near-zero
- Any aggregation method—symbolic or voting—is bounded by this vanishing gap

**Unifying sentence**:

> "Proposition 1 (BR > 1) explains why self-extraction fails at both ends: at low capability, high BR locks constraints to wrong answers; at high capability, near-perfect agreement (κ → 1) makes BR undefined—there are too few errors for any corrective signal to act upon. **[PENDING Dir-N]**: Oracle best-of-K data for Qwen3-14B thinking → confirms oracle gap ≈ 3pp or exact value. This determines whether the ceiling is "near-zero" or "structurally zero."

**Key claim**: Stop optimizing test-time aggregation for reasoning tasks; invest in trained reasoning capabilities.

> "For practitioners, the aggregation ceiling implies a clear resource allocation: one Qwen3-14B thinking trace (83.28%) outperforms twelve Mistral-7B traces aggregated by any method we tested---SC (54.41%), SICA (≈54%), or oracle-FOL (85.78%)---while costing approximately 5--10× a single non-thinking inference but far less than 12× inference plus constraint extraction. - 1 Mistral-7B trace: ~0.5s, baseline cost

- Resource allocation conclusion: training-time investment >> test-time scaling
